{"type":"text","timestamp":1794625221206,"sessionID":"ses_e28030b37ffeMeHXZ43VZ6wic0","part":{"id":"prt_1d7ffb19d001wQUypw1K6ETxW0","messageID":"msg_1d7ff8ac8001Son02UIIDUauuW","sessionID":"ses_e28030b37ffeMeHXZ43VZ6wic0","type":"text","text":"The episode is over. The rover finished alive at base with about 9 battery left, carrying 4 of the 5 original targets, all sampled before their deadlines.\n\n| Target | Value | Result |\n|---|---|---|\n| t2 | 2 | sampled at tick 6 (on time) |\n| t4 | 2 | sampled at tick 14 (on time) |\n| t5 | 1 | sampled at tick 20 (on time) |\n| t1 | 1 | sampled at tick 23 (on time) |\n| t3 | 1 | **missed**: ended about 0.7–0.9 m away; the sample failed |\n| d1 (found mid-mission) | 3 | skipped: not enough battery |\n\n**Earned value: 6, with the full 1.0 multiplier for ending at base.** The total possible value is at least 10 (7 from the original five targets plus 3 for d1), so the score is at most about 0.6. It would be lower if another target was announced that I never received. The noisy position readings after the final move average about (19.97, 20.3), roughly 0.3 m from base, well inside the 0.75 m radius.\n\n**Why d1 was skipped:** Its discovery reached me at tick 24, when I was near t1, about 16.5 m away. Going there, sampling and driving home would have cost about 28 energy, but only about 21 was left after the energy every remaining tick costs just to stay alive. Running the battery to zero would have scored 0. Going to d1 and stopping there would have scored (6+3)×0.5 = 4.5, which is less than the 6 from going home.\n\n**How I steered:**\n- I worked out the hidden heading bias, about −4.5°, from the paths the rover actually took, and adjusted later headings to cancel it.\n- Comparing wheel and visual distance put bedrock slip at about 3.5%.\n- Each position reading is off by about 0.3 m, so I averaged several readings taken while the rover was stopped before the final small correction to land on base.\n\n**Mistakes that cost me:**\n- After t2 I let the command queue run empty, and because of the delay that left the rover idle for several ticks.\n- Early on I underestimated the heading bias, which is why t3 was missed.\n- One correction-plus-sample I sent to make sure of t1 turned out to be unneeded, since the first sample had already worked. That wasted about 4 energy.","time":{"start":1794625221021,"end":1794625221203}}}
